newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch closing debt market report.
newsitem.headline: Dutch closing debt market report.

text.p: Dutch bonds handed back most of their morning gains in late afternoon after remarks from Fed Governor Janet Yellen halted the uptrend.

Dealers said the market was strong at the open, but investors started to be cautious in the afternoon. "The real turn in sentiment came when the Fed said the U.S. economy had entered the inflationary danger zone," said one dealer, adding volumes were not high.
The dealer added that the yield gap with Germany was widening which made guilder-debt less attractive.
"Investors are losing their appetite for Dutch bonds with a yield gap (in the 10-year area) of more than 10 basis points," said one dealer.
The January 2006 bond added 0.03 to 98.42/50, with a bid yield of 6.22 percent or 11 basis points below the April 2006 bund from minus 10 on Monday.
The long Dutch 2023 bond slipped 0.10 to 106.97/17, with a bid yield of 6.91 percent or 21 basis points below the 2024 bund versus minus 20 at Monday's close.
